sections.text: Tactile Luxury The First Touch Customers Comment On Velvet adds a tactile cue before the box opens, but the sourcing decision is technical: flocked and fabric-wrapped surfaces behave differently at corners, curves and logos. Pile direction also changes how colour reads under photography and retail lighting. Ribbon may be printed or solid colour and supplied as a loose tie or controlled pre-tied assembly. sections.heading: Flocked or Fabric-Wrapped? Decide This Before Colour
sections.text: Material Decision Flocked or Fabric-Wrapped? Decide This Before Colour There are two different ways to put velvet on a rigid box, and they fail in different places. Getting this wrong is the reason a box can look right in a photo and wrong in the hand. Flocking bonds short fibres to an adhesive-coated surface, creating a continuous velvet-like layer across panels and formed details. Fibre, adhesive, coverage and substrate all affect hand feel and wear, so approve the production-intent material rather than specifying quality from pile length alone. Fabric-wrapped velvet is woven velvet laminated over the board. The pile is deeper and it drapes, but every corner is a folded or mitred join — under raking light you can see them, and on a small box those joins land close together where the eye is already looking. sections.heading: Use a Textile Reference for Velvet Colour Approval
sections.text: Colour Control Use a Textile Reference for Velvet Colour Approval A coated-paper colour reference and a textile colour reference are not interchangeable. Paper, flock and woven velvet reflect light differently, so a shared colour name does not guarantee the same visual result across the box, ribbon and printed accessories. For sourcing, send a textile-system reference or a physical swatch for velvet, plus the appropriate print reference for paper components . If the set combines a flocked box and printed belly band, approve them side by side under agreed lighting and record which component is the visual master. One more thing photographers hit: velvet pile lies in a direction. The same box shot from two angles reads light in one frame and dark in the other. That is nap, not a defect. Ask for lid and base pile to run the same way, and approve your sample under the lighting you intend to shoot in — not under warehouse fluorescents.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Does velvet flatten or show finger marks? Pile direction, fibre density, colour and handling all affect visible marks. Approve the selected velvet under your retail and photography lighting, and define acceptable appearance with the physical sample. Can the ribbon be printed with our brand? Yes. Supply the artwork, ribbon width, colour reference and preferred tie style. Print registration, colour and bow position should be approved on a sample before bulk production. What is the MOQ for custom velvet boxes? Minimum quantity depends on the box size, velvet construction, colour route, ribbon, insert and decoration. Send the full specification and target quantity so feasibility can be confirmed before quotation. How is a logo applied to velvet? Possible methods include debossing and foil, but suitability depends on whether the surface is flocked or fabric-wrapped, the pile depth and the artwork. Confirm the method on the selected material sample. Can the box hold a multi-piece set? Yes. A tailored insert can position bottles, jars, candles or accessories. Send product dimensions, weights and the preferred removal experience so the insert can be engineered and sampled.
